slides.title: The Professional Home of Medical Affairs Online
bullets: Gathers HCPs, researchers, scientific societies and patient organizations
Professional tone sets it apart from generalist social networks
For an MSL, a natural extension of field activity, not a substitute

slides.title: Follow to Understand the Conversation
bullets: Follow priority KOLs and DOLs in your territory
Watch what content they share and what gets attention
A rich source for emerging clinical thinking and insights
Feeds the same insight capture framework used elsewhere

slides.title: A Profile That Builds Trust Before You Speak
bullets: Clear institutional affiliation and a distinct MSL role
Never confusable with a commercial position
Occasional scientific commentary, never product promotion
Builds credibility organically over time

slides.title: Engaging With Others' Content Is the Delicate Part
bullets: Substantive, evidence-based comments on relevant publications
Congratulating a colleague or starting a scientific conversation
Same rules apply: clear affiliation, professional tone, evidence-based
No appearance of promotion outside approved channels

slides.title: Know Your Organization's Digital Policy
bullets: Applies to LinkedIn as it does to any digital channel
Defines what can be shared without prior review
Defines what requires MLR approval
Protects both the MSL and the organization

takeaway.title: LinkedIn extends the MSL's scientific presence when used for listening, credibility and careful interaction
bullets: Listening to KOLs and DOLs surfaces real insights and trends
A clear, non-commercial profile is the foundation of digital trust
Every interaction follows the same evidence and compliance rules as the field
